headline: Endurance takes November.
deck: Thirteen candidates, seven ballots, and the first dead heat at the top the club has had to actually break — one head-to-head vote decided the winner.
intro: All — seven of you ranked thirteen candidates this round. Endurance (Lansing) and Say Nothing (Keefe) finished level on 58 points, so for the first time the tiebreaker settled the winner rather than a placing. The Condorcet head-to-head went to Endurance 4–3, and it reads November.
outcome: Winner: Endurance (58, on the head-to-head)   ·   Runner-up: Say Nothing (58)   ·   Relegated: Arrowsmith, Nothing Like It in the World, The Gales of November
discussionLead: Sapiens drew the widest spread of opinion we've had — the section one member named as the best of the book was the section another named as the worst. Harari, for his part, did not attend, so our sharpest criticisms and open questions remain unanswered.
tieIntro: Endurance and Say Nothing both finished on 58 points — a genuine dead heat for first. The methodology calls for a Condorcet head-to-head: ignore everything else on the ballot and ask how each voter ranked these two against one another.
tieVerdict: Four of seven put Endurance above Say Nothing, so Endurance takes November on the head-to-head. This is as close as our method can get without breaking: one voter switching the pair reverses the whole result. Say Nothing stays on the candidate list at full strength and starts December as the book to beat.
notes: The tiebreaker decided the book, not a placing. Previous ties (February 2026, August 2026, the three-way in October) all landed below the winner's line or fell through to first-place votes. This one was for first, and the Condorcet head-to-head separated it cleanly on the first pass — no fall-through needed.

The winner is not a strict Condorcet winner. Endurance beats eleven of its twelve rivals head-to-head and loses only to Something Rich and Strange, 3–4 — which finished fourth on 56 points. Borda is the club's stated method, it named a winner, and the pairwise quirk is recorded here as a curiosity rather than a dispute.

Broad, not unanimous. Endurance took two first-place votes — the most in the field — and also one last-place vote. It won on being ranked high by most and buried by one, rather than on consensus. Say Nothing, by contrast, was never anyone's last choice.

Four debut books, four different fates. Endurance, Something Rich and Strange, Born to Run and Arrowsmith all appeared on a ballot for the first time. They finished first, fourth, fifth — and relegated.
The River of Doubt reaches twenty-one polls and finished tenth, one place clear of the relegation line.
